You say pursuant to the order of the Main Staff of the 15th of July, 1993, on the same day you request accurate data on troop deployment, specifying the data on the location of your units, et cetera. The last paragraph: "The data needs to be accurate and precise, showing the location of units where your forces are holding positions." What prompted you to draft this order to all of the units?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR MILOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, it is clear that it was requested by the Main Staff. They wanted to have more precise information. Secondly, there must have been inaccuracies in sketching deployments on the map. Therefore, everyone had to verify the position of their forces so as to reflect those positions accurately on the map. Even the most minute details had to be taken into account when displaying it on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have this admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D2840, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have a look at P1763.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It's a whole year later, that is to say, July 1994. Why was it necessary to reissue this type of order? We saw the one in September 1992. That's when it was issued for the first time.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR MILOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if you understood me properly at the beginning when I started discussing the system of control and command. The system of command and control is an activity which needs to be improved constantly and worked on. Objectively speaking, there may be inadequacies even when there is very strong insistence on abiding by it. In this case, I did not want to have any kind of lack of clarity or something that may result in insufficient information on the situation. It was very important that the system was properly functioning. There were constant needs to caution, warn, and improve the functioning of the system. There were weaknesses and problems that occurred from time to time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What was the importance of such reports for the commander?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR MILOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He cannot make appropriate decisions if he lacks clear indicators and if he has inaccurate information.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. It says that lately all documents are being drafted by commands in a stereotypical way on behalf of the commander. Dead-lines were not being met. Work was not being done properly. And we have received orders asking for specific data that need to be honoured.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR MILOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is all correct.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we go to the last page to see if you signed it and this has already been admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Immediately following this document you took over command; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR MILOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have 1D7537 to see what things were like in early April 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: At the time you were the corps commander; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR MILOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D7537.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Could we just go back to that first -- the document we've just been dealing with, D2840. I think it dates from 1993 rather than 1994.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, that was my understanding.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: General, this is April 1995. It says: "Despite the warning that you had received earlier you still failed to fulfil your regular planned obligations regarding monthly reports ..." and so on and so forth. So this is another warning. General, until the very end of the war, was there such thing as full control and -- of the reporting system within the system of command and control? Were there always problems or were you successful in implementing it in full by the end of the war?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR MILOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we see this is already 1995, so my answer would be no. I know that the system that was in place could ensure that we worked normally, and any kind of intervention of this nature was simply an expression of the need to have it improved or to do away with shortcomings. Since I know how the entire situation ended, I believe that the system towards the end functioned meticulously.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. General, were you satisfied with the number of professional officers in lower commanding positions and did that have any impact on problems discussed in documents like this one?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR MILOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's very relative who you are satisfied with or not. What my aim was to have the people do their best given their ability and given the circumstances. Anything beyond that was even better and assistance was provided. I tried to respect everyone because not every person had the same ability and knowledge. Every one of them was precious for the functioning of the system even with their weaknesses, their flaws, if there were any.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: As per establishment, how many professional officers were you supposed to have at junior levels and how many did you have, in fact?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR MILOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we simply put that aside. We no longer wanted to follow the establishment. We fought for all personnel that had been highly trained, especially those who had attended the command staff academy. To a certain extent we were successful but not too much because the corps command was short of officers who had a different range of abilities. The brigade commanders were the people who knew their job and it was a comfort to me. Veljko Stojanovic, who was a moderate commander, and he managed to defend an area that not many people would be able to. The same goes for Dragan Josipovic who resembled a chess player when assessing the enemy and awaiting the enemy's mistake to act. It was all up to scratch. The same goes for Vlado Lizdek. The staff I had -- well, I'm grateful to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted? And I'd like to conclude for the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Conclude for the day. You need how much to conclude your direct examination? We'll admit this.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D2841, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A session, Your Excellency. I have three areas to cover, half of this one and another two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, there's -- there should be a limit. The Chamber will give you half an hour tomorrow to conclude your direct examination. I think that's more than reasonable. Mr. Robinson, my understanding was that Mr. Krstic's evidence was fixed on the 4th of February. Was there any change?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: There hasn't been any official change yet, Mr. President, but I was going to ask you in light of the delay of this testimony to postpone that to later in the week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, any observation?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, I need to go over the projected schedule, including the projected cross-examination, which I imagine is a factor that Mr. Robinson is considering. But I take his point -- I take it his point is a very practical one. If there's no other reason he wishes to adjust the schedule other than the time he imagines it will take us to reach that witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So apparently we have to just determine where we are given the projections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So who is going to inform him and how?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I think the best thing to do would be to wait until tomorrow and see how things progress, but at some point, perhaps the Trial Chamber can make an order or else we can inform General Krstic and his counsel of the schedule. I know that the order said that the subpoena was for the 4th of February or a time thereafter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm not sure whether I can do it in two minutes. The Chamber will now issue its decision on the accused's 76th motion for finding of disclosure violation filed on the 14th of January, 2013, having considered the Prosecution response filed on 28th of January. The motion concerns an UNPROFOR report which was disclosed to the accused in December 2012. The accused asserts that this report was in the Prosecution's possession for a number of years and that its late disclosure amounts to a violation of Rule 68 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, and the obligation to disclose exculpatory material contained therein. As a remedy for the violation the accused seeks, one, an express finding that the Prosecution violated Rule 68; two, that witness Thorbjorn Overgard be re-called to be questioned on the report; and three, that the report be admitted from the bar table. The Chamber finds that the Prosecution violated Rule 68 by its failure to disclose the report which it finds to be potentially exculpatory. The Chamber reminds the Prosecution that such errors should have been identified and rectified well before the date of disclosure of the document which has been in its possession for a number of years. However, having reviewed the content of the document in light of other similar documents, such as Exhibit P1201, P1782, and P5943, which were available to the accused, and the line of questioning already pursued on the issue this report relates to, the Chamber finds that the accused was not prejudiced by the late disclosure. In the absence of prejudice, there is no basis to grant the accused's request that Witness Thorbjorn Over gard be re-called. Having said that, the Chamber is satisfied that the accused has adequately contextualised and explained how the report fits into his case. The Chamber is also satisfied as to its relevance and probative value and notes that it bears sufficient indicia of authenticity for admission from the bar table. The Chamber, therefore, admits the report into evidence from the bar table and instructs the Registry to assign it an exhibit number once it has been uploaded on e-court. However, on my part, I refer to my partially dissenting opinion in the Chamber's decision on the accused's 37th to 42nd disclosure violation motions of 29th of March, 2011, and decline to make a finding of violation in the absence of prejudice to the accused. Shall we give the number?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Um, if I may, that document was already admitted today during the course of General Milosevic's examination. Mr. Reid is just trying to find the number for me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. The hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 30th day of January, 2013, at 9.00 a.m.
